# Brain tumor detection from MRI (tumor vs no tumor)

> A fine-tuned EfficientNetB0 that says whether a brain MRI scan shows a tumor. Compared against a custom CNN and a frozen VGG16 baseline. The model runs in the browser on this site with ONNX Runtime Web. Student project, not a medical device.

## Links

- Live website: https://brain-tumor-detection-sigma-eight.vercel.app
- GitHub repository: https://github.com/zartashhaiderr-stack/brain-tumor-detection
- Dataset (Kaggle, Brain Tumor MRI Dataset by Masoud Nickparvar): https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/masoudnickparvar/brain-tumor-mri-dataset
- Model weights (ONNX, used by this site): https://brain-tumor-detection-sigma-eight.vercel.app/model/brain_tumor_effnetb0.onnx
- Model config and test metrics (JSON): https://brain-tumor-detection-sigma-eight.vercel.app/project.json
- Training notebook: https://github.com/zartashhaiderr-stack/brain-tumor-detection/blob/main/notebooks/brain_tumor_detection_colab.ipynb
- Prediction script: https://github.com/zartashhaiderr-stack/brain-tumor-detection/blob/main/predict.py

## Test results (EfficientNetB0, 1,584 test scans)

- Sensitivity (tumors caught): 96.45%
- Specificity (healthy scans cleared): 100%
- Accuracy: 97.35%
- ROC-AUC: 0.998
- Decision threshold: 0.5

## Model input and output

- Input: RGB image resized to 224 x 224, raw pixels 0 to 255, float32, shape [N, 224, 224, 3]. No normalization.
- Output: tumor_probability from 0 to 1. Tumor when at or above the threshold.
